messages.subject: Summary.scantwo
parts:
Hi Karl:
I use the following command to analyze two-locus interactions only at
marker positons:
> out.two <- scantwo(data,pheno.col=1,method='imp',incl.markers=T)
> summary(out.two)
Then, only one interaction displayed in the results between the markers
at one chromosome and another chromosome. e.g. like this:
c1:c1 150 50
c1:c2 80 20
c1:c3 ...

How to show interactions between all markers with a special criteria?
In another word, maybe there are more than one interactions between
markers at chr1 and markers at chr2, how to show them all? like this:
c1:c1 150 50
c1:c1 150 100
c1:c2 80 20
c1:c2 80 100
c1:c3 ...

messages.author: ab8dbe3bec292afe
messages.subject: Re: Summary.scantwo
parts:
summary.scantwo picks out just a single point from each chromosome pair
(just as summary.scanone picks out just a single point from each
chromosome).

If you want to look at further details, you need to study the
contents of
the out.two object itself. out.two$lod is a matrix with all of the
LOD scores.

karl
